# Vendored decimal sources

Two upstream projects, both taken whole and unmodified, used by
`fp/decimal.cpp` for the text side of the vertical slice (plan section 5.3).

## `fast_float/` - decimal text to binary32

Upstream: <https://github.com/fastfloat/fast_float>
Commit: `f103228650b1b3ca4363ebb9a6caee20179a2390` (2026-09-23)
Licence: MIT (also offered as Apache-2.0 or BSL-1.0; all three texts are here)

Header-only. `fast_float::from_chars` parses the whole text with round-to-nearest,
ties-to-even, correctly rounded to the destination type, locale-independently -
exactly the contract plan 5.3 asks for. Only the headers are vendored; the
repository's tests and benchmarks are not.

## `ryu/` - binary32 to shortest decimal text

Upstream: <https://github.com/ulfjack/ryu>
Commit: `4c0618b0e44f7ef027ebae05d2cc7812048f7c8f` (2026-02-09)
Licence: Apache-2.0 or BSL-1.0 (both texts are here)

`f2s.c` (plus `common.h`, `digit_table.h`, `f2s_intrinsics.h`,
`f2s_full_table.h`) produces the shortest decimal string that round-trips
through binary32. It writes Ryu's own notation (`3.14E0`), so `decimal.cpp`
reads the digits and the decimal exponent back out of that buffer and renders
its own formats; the *digits* are Ryu's, which is the part that guarantees
shortest-round-trip.

## Why both directions are separate from the kernel

The kernel never sees text: it takes and returns bit patterns, and SoftFloat
has no string conversion (plan 5.3). Parsing happens once, when an editor
commits, and the instance's configuration keeps the resulting `uint32_t bits`.
Display formats on the CPU and hands the finished string to the renderer.

## Re-vendoring

Copy the same file sets from the two upstream checkouts, update the commit
hashes above, and run `tests/float-package.ps1`: the decimal vectors in
`tests/data/float32/` are generated by `tools/float-decimal-vectors.py`, which
does not use either library, so a change in their behaviour shows up as failing
vectors rather than as silently different text.
